articles.body: Oklahoma’s Republican governor warned against populist economic ideas gaining popularity, as he called for fellow Republicans to reject socialism and embrace free markets and an “ownership economy.” “A socialist or a populist economy is something that is not American,” Gov. Kevin Stitt said in an interview on Wednesday at the POLITICO Pub, on the sidelines of the National Governors Association's New Governors Leadership Forum in Deer Valley, Utah. “We should all be concerned about the amount of people that think that socialism is the answer.” When asked if he was concerned about socialist tendencies on the right, Stitt criticized fellow Republicans who have called for data center moratoriums.. “When you start dictating … you see some people from the far right saying, ‘Well, we don’t want data centers. We don’t want that,’” Stitt said. “When did we become a party that if you follow all the rules, you follow the permitting, the clean water, the clean air, and you own your own land, that we allow the government to tell you what you can do on that property?” the Oklahoma governor asked. “That is what I'm talking about, that we need to be very, very careful about.” Stitt also called on President Donald Trump to use his final two years in the White House to push for bipartisan immigration reform — his latest remarks on the topic. “We need to have a strong border. We need to know who is coming into our country. We need to vet those people,” Stitt told POLITICO’s Samuel Benson. “He can lead on this, he can fix this immigration policy. “To me, we are overthinking it,” Stitt added. “It is as simple as: If an employer is vouching for an employee, the state governors should be able to issue that workforce permit. Period, end of story.” Stitt described Trump as a “business person” who “understands the need for a workforce.” But he blamed Congress and other interests in Washington for standing in the way of reform. “It's not that complicated. But the problem is Washington, D.C., each side thinks they're winning on it. They raise money off of it. They politic off of it. They try to crush the other side over these issues instead of fixing it for the American people,” Stitt said. “That's why you saw this huge swing in the midterms.”
articles.headline: Oklahoma GOP governor warns of growing socialist tendencies on the right

articles.body: Utah’s Republican governor wants his party to move beyond President Donald Trump heading into the next presidential election. “It’s time for the next thing,” Gov. Spencer Cox said in an interview on Wednesday at the POLITICO Pub, on the sidelines of the National Governors Association’s New Governors Leadership Forum in Deer Valley, Utah. Cox called on his fellow Republicans to start looking for new leadership in the wake of this month’s midterm election defeats. “This is how this works when presidents move on. We should be looking for the next leadership in our party and what that looks like,” Cox told POLITICO’s Samuel Benson. “We’ve got JD Vance and Marco Rubio, and those seem to be kind of the two choices now,” Cox said, referring to the Vice President and Secretary of State, respectively. “But I think you’ll see a lot of people step up … there are a lot of really interesting folks.” “I’m a fan of governors,” Cox added. “I think governors with executive experience are the best to lead the country.” Vance told Fox News earlier this week that he would decide “sometime next year” whether he will run for president in 2028. Rubio has dismissed suggestions that he would launch his own bid, and has said he would support Vance if the Vice President ran for the White House. “I am hopeful that there are some Republican governors that will throw their hat in,” said Cox, a two-term governor. “We can have a competition of ideas heading in to find out what's next.” Cox said that Trump still has a “really important role to play” in leading the party over the next two years, adding that the president still had an “opportunity” to strike bipartisan deals on permitting reform and other policy areas in his last two years in office. Cox called the president “unique,” adding: “He’s someone who has the attention of the country in a way that almost no president has had in my lifetime.” “People really love him or really don’t like him, but everybody’s paying attention to him,” he said.
articles.headline: Utah GOP governor on Trump and 2028: ‘It’s time for the next thing’

articles.body: Deb Haaland is about to take the helm of a newly-minted Democratic presidential primary battleground. She has thoughts for her party’s White House hopefuls on how to win there. Haaland, New Mexico’s incoming governor, told POLITICO that immigration will be a “top issue” in the presidential election — one that she’s “anxious” to see how future candidates plan to address — and said that engaging with rural voters in her state will be key to any successful primary campaign. “New Mexico is the fifth largest state, and we are largely rural,” Haaland told POLITICO’s Erin Doherty in an onstage interview at the National Governors Association's New Governors Leadership Forum in Utah. “There are far more rural communities than there are large cities in our state, and so this will be important for New Mexicans to to really understand or to really know that any presidential candidate understands the challenges that they're facing.” Immigration is “going to be a top issue with the 2028 presidential election,” she added. “New Mexico is an early primary state, and it happens that we're a border state, too.” Haaland’s ascension to the governor’s mansion coincides with a major change in New Mexico’s place in the Democratic Party's presidential nominating calendar pecking order. The state will now be fourth in the voting calendar behind South Carolina, Nevada and New Hampshire. The move gives New Mexicans — and their new governor — significant influence in shaping the kind of nominee the party selects to take back the White House. It’ll also pose a significant test for candidate’s engagement with Latino voters, as New Mexico ranks first nationwide in its population share of Latino residents. Some of those potential candidates have already come calling. “Rahm Emanuel was in New Mexico, and he did quite a bit of traveling around,” Haaland said, noting that several senators made their own sojourns to the state for an event hosted in October by Democratic Sen. Ben Ray Luján in Alberquerque. Former Secretary of Transportation Pete Buttigieg made his own trip to the state in September. “Whether all of them are running for president, I can't tell you, but I am really anxious to see who does.” Haaland, a former Secretary of the Interior and the first Native American woman elected to a governorship, is ready to wield her own influence in the process as well, flexing her new power broker status . “I would love to endorse, but I'll wait and see who throws their hat in the ring,” she said. Haaland was swept into office with a historic number of fellow Democrats across the country on a mandate to deliver on affordability. It’s the “biggest issue” in New Mexico, Haaland said, adding that her priority to deliver lower costs for New Mexicans will start with expanding access to affordable health care. “Right now we're talking with some of the leaders in the legislature about health care, a public option for people in New Mexico,” she said. “Health care is a top top priority.”
articles.headline: This new early-state governor has advice for 2028 Democratic hopefuls

articles.body: Bo French, the far-right firebrand who centered his losing campaign for the Texas Railroad Commission on his anti-immigration stance, lost his membership at a Fort Worth country club, according to a letter obtained by POLITICO . The letter from River Crest Country Club, dated Nov. 10 and addressed to French, said the club’s board of directors voted to terminate French’s membership immediately “for reasons relating to the reputation and general welfare of the Club.” French said Wednesday on social media that the board asked him to resign in September due to "racist posts." He said he refused to do so, leading to an expulsion meeting. "Nothing I said in September was racist," he said in a published statement that he read to the board. The country club, founded in 1911, is the eighth to open in the state and boasts being a “who’s who” of Fort Worth. It hosts a 6,368-yard golf course that has been a training ground for top golfers, according to its website. River Crest declined to comment, citing its policy of not doing so about “past, present and prospective members” and club operations, its general manager said in an email. French, who has a history of making controversial statements on immigration issues like the H-1B visa program, made headlines in September after going viral on social media for a post he made that appeared to disparage Asian American students at the University of Texas at Austin. His remarks capitalized on the growing anti-Indian sentiment sweeping Texas and across the nation , particularly against holders of the high-skilled worker visa, a majority of whom are from India. The post quickly drew rebukes from Democrats and some Texas Republicans, who denounced it as racist. But French stood by the post . He said he was criticizing admission and hiring policies at UT, the state’s public flagship, that he claimed discriminated against Texas residents. (State law requires a majority of admitted students at the school to be residents of the state.) French lost by 677,000 votes in his bid to sit on the influential statewide body that regulates Texas’ oil and gas industry two months later amid a statewide wipeout for the GOP. He previously led the Tarrant County Republican Party and also had two unsuccessful state House bids. French did not respond to requests for comment sent to multiple email addresses associated with him. Ashley Ahn contributed reporting.
articles.headline: Bo French loses Texas country club membership

articles.body: Sen. Bernie Moreno isn’t sugarcoating things. The incoming chair of the National Republican Senatorial Committee will be in charge of defending 19 GOP seats in 2028 — and he’ll need to flip at least six more to regain control of the Senate majority. “Looking at it right now, it's absolutely a savagely brutal map,” the Ohio Republican said in an interview on Capitol Hill. After a historic midterms shellacking, Moreno is in the hot seat as he looks to navigate his chamber — and the party — through a rebuilding of its brand and its base over next two years. Republicans will likely have just 44 seats heading into 2028. They need to hold onto seats in battleground states like Wisconsin and North Carolina, while trying to flip seats held by Democratic Sens. Mark Kelly in Arizona, John Fetterman in Pennsylvania, Raphael Warnock in Georgia and Catherine Cortez Masto in Nevada. Moreno and his team have interviewed a handful of candidates over the last few days to be the next NRSC executive director, according to four people with direct knowledge of the matter, granted anonymity to discuss private conversations. Republicans expect Chris Grant, a former Moreno and Trump campaign staffer who now runs his own firm, to serve as a main outside GOP consultant for the committee. On top of the grueling map ahead, the Ohio Republican is facing the additional task of working with a lame duck president who still wields immense power over the GOP and its primaries. Then there’s the vice president, who is likely to run for president himself in the same two-year sprint. Moreno is close with both of those men. Asked how involved he expects the White House to be in GOP primaries and recruiting going forward, he replied, “We’re going to work on all of that.” It’ll be a complicated path forward. Moreno, over the past cycle has been unwilling to cast blame on President Donald Trump or Vice President JD Vance. Days before the midterm elections, he said if Republicans lost, it would be because people were “pissed off” about high gas prices. He’s unlikely to completely distance himself and the NRSC brand from the president's influence. But the party is currently undergoing a reckoning of how closely to align with the president after voters delivered an uncompromising rebuke of Trump’s economic agenda. Across the country, several battlegrounds and once-thought-to-be-safe red territory fell to Democratic hands. Trump in the 2026 cycle angered many Senate Republicans by supporting a primary challenge against Sen. John Cornyn of Texas — a move they privately say cost them north of $200 million as they tried, in vain, to save Ken Paxton’s imperiled campaign. The president also supported a primary challenge against Sen. Bill Cassidy of Louisiana, and pushed Sen. Thom Tillis to decide to retire in highly competitive North Carolina. One of the biggest challenges before Moreno and Senate Republicans after the midterms wipeout is to find candidates who can win a general election in highly competitive states, while also making it through GOP primaries where Trump will be a major factor. They’ll need to push back on the White House if the president tries, once again, to intervene — though that’s easier said than done. “There will be no patience for bad recruits this cycle,” said one senior Republican granted anonymity to discuss internal conversations, referring to the implosions of Paxton, Michael Whatley in North Carolina and other Republicans who were hand-picked by Trump. The White House referred POLITICO to Trump's post-midterms comments, where he blamed his party’s losses on the fact that he wasn’t on the ballot and said he brought several candidates "closer to victory," though they ultimately lost. Senate Majority Leader John Thune — who will be the minority leader next year — and his team plan to be heavily involved in recruitment efforts, according to two people involved in the conversations, granted anonymity to speak candidly. Their goal, one of the people said, is “to make sure we have our strongest possible candidates on the ballot in 2028.” Moreno is already trying to find a GOP recruit in his home state of Ohio to run against incoming Democratic Sen. Sherrod Brown, whose term will be up again in 2028 after he won a special election against GOP Sen. Jon Husted earlier this month. The new NRSC chair said he’s looking for “somebody who can beat the crap out of Sherrod Brown.” Husted in private conversations hasn’t completely ruled out another bid, but he’s indicated he’s unlikely to run again, according to three people with knowledge of the matter, granted anonymity to speak candidly. Ohio Republicans expect former state Sen. Kevin Coughlin to explore a potential Senate bid. And they’re watching Rep. Mike Turner (R-Ohio), who just lost his reelection. Husted did not respond to a request for comment. A Turner spokesperson said in a statement that the representative "has been approached by several people about this and is keeping all his options open.” If Vance doesn’t seek his own presidential bid, Republicans in his home state are holding a long-shot hope that he, too, might consider a return to his old job. “JD Vance would be a dream candidate,” said one Ohio Republican. articles.body: Nearly twice as many Americans expect a Democrat to win the presidency in 2028 than they do a Republican, a new POLITICO Poll finds . Even one in five of President Donald Trump’s own 2024 voters believe Republicans will lose the White House, a bad sign for the GOP as it struggles to recover from widespread losses this cycle and figure out its identity after spending a decade orbiting around Trump. Just 60% of Trump voters believe Republicans will keep the White House. Democratic voters are far more confident about their own party, according to the survey conducted by PF Global in the days after the midterm: Among voters who backed Kamala Harris, 87% expect Democrats to win in 2028. Beneath the unity is disagreement over what kind of nominee to pick. Pluralities of voters agree the next president should be a fighter when asked to choose from a list of qualities. But voters across the ideological spectrum also said they want other things from the country’s 48th president. While 43% of Harris voters want “a fighter,” 40% also selected “a progressive” and 34% chose “creative.” Among Trump voters, the 45% said they want to see “a conservative” elected president, surpassing the 39% who picked “a fighter.” They're also divided over what background their nominees should come from. Nearly three in 10 Trump voters say they would prefer the next president be someone who has not worked in Trump’s administration. That number rises to 46% among Trump voters who don’t identify as MAGA, whereas 82% of his loyal MAGA base would prefer the next president be someone who did work for Trump. That debate is playing out in real-time among top GOP leaders and lawmakers. More and more Hill Republicans are eyeing Secretary of State Marco Rubio for 2028, who they say is less associated with the midterm bloodbath than Vice President JD Vance. Others say the nominee should be someone entirely outside of Trump’s direct orbit. “As much as I like Rubio, and as much as I like Vance, they can't be our nominee,” said Dan McMaster, the chair of Michigan’s Shiawassee County Republican Party. “We need to get a Republican as far away from Trump as possible, and even then, I think it's going to be a battle.” “You've got to have some fresh blood in there, and you've got to have someone that has some distance from the crap that's gone on the last two years,” said one GOP strategist who worked on multiple House races last cycle and was granted anonymity to speak candidly about their own party. In a statement, Natalie Baldassarre, a spokesperson for the Republican National Committee, said the president isn’t going anywhere. "President Trump remains the unequivocal leader of our party who's cut taxes, lowered drug costs, and secured our border,” Baldassarre said. “Republicans will continue to harness his ability to energize our base and expose the Democrats' disastrous record to win in 2028." The White House also pointed POLITICO to separate polling earlier this month that shows Trump’s approval rating sits at 75% with all Republicans and jumps to 93% with those who identify as MAGA. “President Trump will never stop delivering results for the American people and he will undoubtedly go down as the most successful and consequential president in American history,” said Davis Ingle, a White House spokesperson. On election night earlier this month, Trump blamed his party’s losses on the fact that he wasn’t on the ballot, telling POLITICO by phone , “I wasn't on the ballot. If I was on the ballot, we would have won; we would have won it all very easily.” Meanwhile, Democrats have their own disagreements to figure out as they select their nominee. This cycle’s blue wave has bolstered the progressive wing of the party, which has long hoped to prove their candidates can win in purple battlegrounds, not just in safe-blue states. But the poll reveals skepticism remains — at least among moderates — over whether progressive wins in 2026 can translate to the presidential stage in 2028. The survey found a majority of progressive Democrats — 63% — want a progressive to be president, compared with just 23% of moderates who say the same. Half of progressive Democrats are convinced that being a progressive is a quality that will get their candidate elected in 2028. Moderates are less certain of that, though they’re also not as confident in their own faction: Just 37% think being a moderate is a quality that ensures the Democratic candidate wins. “Whoever's running for president has seen what's happened and also has seen the power of our movement, and so this is something that could be carried on to 2028,” said progressive New Jersey Democratic Rep.-elect Adam Hamawy, reflecting on the wins he and others enjoyed this cycle. “Despite it being the most expensive elections in history, we showed that people are able to beat out money when we come together.” And with Democrats winning Senate seats in deep-red states like Kansas and Mississippi for the first time in decades, many now argue that the entire map is in play for 2028. The poll found that 60% of Democrats think the party should focus their efforts on winning all states in the presidential election, even ones that seemed like deep Republican areas, rather than focus on holding the states where they know their supporters are. Republicans felt the same, with 56% also arguing for an “all states” approach as the party races to rebuild in territory they once thought was safe. “I have been very, very loud about the fact that the path to the presidency leads through the South,” said Democratic strategist Dallas Jones, who ran statewide Black voter engagement for Lone Star Rising PAC, the outside group that supported Texas Sen.-elect James Talarico. “But again, we don't make investments there. We're playing the same electoral map with the same swing states.”

articles.body: Outgoing Sen. John Cornyn sees the Nvidia scandal and questions about the Trump administration’s alleged lax chip export control rules as part of a broader perception of corruption, which he said contributed to the Republican drubbing in the midterms. “Let’s talk about Nvidia and export controls,” the Texas Republican said when asked to name examples of corruption he sees at the federal level during an onstage interview at the Atlantic Summit on Tuesday. He then pointed to media reports that advanced Nvidia chips may have been diverted to China through the Singapore-based company Megaspeed, and that the Commerce Department, led by Secretary Howard Lutnick, resisted efforts by other Cabinet agencies to crack down on Megaspeed. “I just think there’s a lot of things that will be investigated, and we’ll learn more about, basically, this perception that there was self-dealing going on that I think caused a lot of unease by the American people,” Cornyn said. He said President Donald Trump is at the center of the perceived corruption — “the buck stops with him” — and that many congressional Republicans, fearing the White House’s retribution, have chosen not to cross the president publicly. Cornyn’s remarks come as fallout from the Nvidia turmoil that led to CEO Jensen Huang’s ouster continues to roil Washington. The Trump administration is scrambling to further restrict China’s access to the most advanced American chips as pressure mounts from Capitol Hill, which is also set to hear testimony from Huang and Lutnick in the coming weeks. The four-term senator, who lost his primary earlier this year to the Trump-endorsed Ken Paxton, did not mince words when asked about the cause of the blue wave that swept even statewide offices across his home state. “Well, President Trump said he was on the ballot.” In a pair of statements, White House spokespeople blamed Democrats for refusing “to do anything to stop waste, fraud, and abuse in our government” and highlighted the Commerce Department’s interim final rule to “crack down on the smuggling of advanced U.S. SI chips, including through third countries and remote access by Chinese SI labs.” “The Trump Administration will continue to take decisive action to protect America’s technological edge, strengthen our national security, and ensure the future of SI is built in America,” White House spokesperson Matthew Middleton said. Cornyn in his remarks Tuesday also urged Washington to keep China as its top national security and foreign policy focus, as Trump is set to meet with China’s leader Xi Jinping later this week. He warned about disruption to the semiconductor supply chain should China try to invade Taiwan, its island democracy neighbor that produces an overwhelming majority of the world’s most advanced chips. “The idea that there could be another pandemic or military conflict or natural disaster that would disrupt that ought to worry everybody,” he said. “That’s one of my principal concerns is what China may or may not do in the Taiwan Straits.”

articles.body: In the days before the midterm election, Rep. Henry Cuellar (D-Texas) felt confident that a blue wave could open the door to immigration reform. Cuellar was so bullish that he reached out to acting Immigration and Customs Enforcement director David Venturella and the Customs and Border Protection commissioner Rodney Scott to feel out areas of “common ground,” he said in an interview. Now Cuellar is one of several moderate Democrats angling to strike a deal with the White House, especially on reining in ICE officers and creating legal pathways to citizenship for some immigrants. They’re undeterred by President Donald Trump’s elevation of immigration hardliner Stephen Miller to chief of staff. And they’re buoyed by Trump’s recent admission that his deportations policy was “too tough.” Several of these Democrats have already placed calls to Trump and DHS secretary Markwayne Mullin to express a willingness to work together. Cuellar said he reached back out to Venturella and Scott after the election to try to schedule meetings. “If the president, as the president of the United States, makes a decision — and not a chief of staff — we can get the job done,” Cuellar said in an interview. “I’m sure we’re going to find a lot of differences, but if we sit down, we can definitely resolve them.” It’ll be a tough road: Securing buy-in from the White House becomes undoubtedly more complicated with Miller, a champion of the administration’s aggressive deportation push. Republicans in Congress have largely been willing to defer to the president on the issue. And Democratic leaders have questioned Trump’s sincerity and said they have no interest in working with Miller. The possibility will become even more tenuous once Democrats begin investigating the Trump administration, including the president’s immigration enforcement agencies. CBP and ICE did not respond to requests for comment. Neither did Democratic leaders Sen. Chuck Schumer and Rep. Hakeem Jeffries. Democrats like Cuellar, Sen.-elects James Talarico of Texas and Annie Andrews of South Carolina are aware of all of those hurdles. But they’re betting the midterms have created an opening for serious talks: Latino voters across the country swung hard back toward Democrats this cycle, and more and more Republicans are recognizing that their immigration agenda hurt them politically. Talarico and Andrews have publicly expressed interest in working with the president on immigration, and both ran on platforms that emphasized creating paths to citizenship for undocumented immigrants. “I’m ready to work with President Trump to fix this broken immigration system,” Talarico said in a statement. Inside the White House, there’s a recognition that the president will proceed however he so chooses, regardless of who the chief of staff is. Trump is accessible to outside voices — journalists, business leaders and lawmakers regularly call him directly — and often poses policy questions to aides and allies as he decides which direction he will go. “Everybody’s like, ‘Well, it’s never going to happen with Stephen Miller.’ Look, Donald Trump’s the president. I don’t care if Stephen Miller’s the chief of staff or Susie Wiles or John Kelly or whoever the chief of staff might be,” said a person close to the White House, granted anonymity to speak about the internal dynamic. For Democrats, there’s a real political incentive to getting a deal done ahead of a critical 2028 presidential election — especially as the party seeks to win back voter trust on immigration and border security, policy areas that spelled doom for them in 2024. “You have these Democrats who flip red states, and it’s also to their self-interest, right? Not just to do rhetoric, and go big or go home, but actually come to the middle with the president, with the Republicans. Because if not, I think that the big lesson this election is, Hispanic voters are gonna flip back ... if they don’t see Democrats delivering anything the next two years,” said Rebecca Shi, the executive director of ABIC, a coalition of pro-immigration reform business executives. She added that there’s a lesson for Republicans, too, if they don’t come to the table: “They will lose the White House.” White House spokesperson Lauren Bis touted Trump’s immigration accomplishments, including border security, a drop in crime and the creation of the Homeland Security Task Force and said the president’s “strong immigration policy remains unchanged.” She said Democrats should work alongside Trump to “keep our southern border secure, remove dangerous illegal criminals from our communities, and stop the illicit trafficking of lethal drugs.” Democrats welcomed the president’s remarks on 60 Minutes on Sunday, when he said he was open to legal pathways for some unauthorized immigrants who haven’t committed crimes and are working and contributing to the economy. Mullin also floated an openness to a bipartisan immigration overhaul involving DACA, which could provide permanent legal status to some undocumented immigrants who arrived in the U.S. as children, even as he — and the president — have insisted that any proposal wouldn’t include amnesty. In a sign that Democrats have learned the lessons of the Biden administration , many of them are eager to pair reforms with border security measures. Cuellar, who will chair the Homeland Security Appropriations subcommittee in the next conference, has long suggested including guardrails on ICE in the next funding bill, such as requiring judicial warrants, rolling out body camera usage and restoring “sensitive locations” such as churches and schools as off-limits. Sen. Ruben Gallego (D-Ariz.), another Democrat who has expressed interest in working with the Trump administration, said that beyond “talk,” it would help to see some smaller concrete policy shifts from the White House to affirm that Trump is, in fact, open to changes to the immigration system. “The way to do that is to have some reforms already at ICE — whether it’s shutting down these detention centers, giving certain level of protections, whether to veterans, so they don't get deported, to maybe parents of U.S. citizens, they don’t get deported — something to show that, you know, it's not just talk, this isn’t going to be a policy led by Stephen Miller,” he said. But Miller remains a bogeyman for Democrats, someone they view as responsible for the president’s most extreme immigration policies. As chief of staff, he can ensure he’s one of the last people in the president’s ear — and that the White House doesn’t bend to what he sees as unrealistic Democratic demands. “The reason why they wouldn’t do an amnesty deal, I believe, is because it would be the ultimate and most public contradiction of the central thesis of this entire political program as it was sold to voters,” said Mike Howell, president of the Oversight Project and a member of the Mass Deportation Coalition. “It would be the end of the America First coalition as it currently exists.” Democrats' distrust of Miller will also make it challenging for them to align on any potential deal with the White House. “Stephen Miller is the mastermind and architect of terror, and death, and illegality in this country, and he is not anyone who even understands truthfully what immigration policy should look like,” said Rep. Sydney Kamlager-Dove (D-Calif). “No deals, man. No deals,” she added. The White House pointed to Miller’s experience on the Hill as a valuable asset. White House spokesperson Taylor Rogers said unlike Democrats “who refused to work with the President and blocked many of his popular policies, Stephen Miller has a track record of spearheading bipartisan efforts: public safety reform, making our cities such as Washington, D.C. and Memphis safe again, drug pricing transparency, and unleashing a nuclear energy renaissance.” Lawmakers are waiting for the president to make the first move. Senate Majority Leader John Thune, who will continue to lead his fellow Republicans when Democrats retake control of the Senate this January, told reporters after the election that “if there's something he wants to do there, we can have that conversation.” “There are always some landmines, which is why in the past the wheels have kind of come off, despite some really good efforts at trying to find a landing spot. But yeah we're open to something he wants to propose,” Thune added. Jordain Carney contributed to this report.

"></img><p>Hay fronteras que no necesitan vallas ni muros para marcar distancias. Basta con cruzar de un lado a otro de la misma ciudad: la renta disponible media en Aravaca, el cógido postal más rico de Madrid, supera en unos 63.000 euros la de Entrevías, que ni siquiera alcanzaba los 20.000 euros en 2024, <a href="https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es/AEAT/Contenidos_Comunes/La_Agencia_Tributaria/Estadisticas/Publicaciones/sites/irpfCodPostal/2024/jrubik240167108bc1f4c2ae7d67122ed45b2639a50d7b.html" rel="">según los últimos datos disponibles</a>. La distancia entre ambas zonas es una de las muchas expresiones de una desigualdad enquistada en España y que, a menos de dos semanas de las elecciones generales del 29-N, ocupa espacios y tonos muy distintos en los programas electorales de los principales partidos, con una fractura muy marcada entre derecha e izquierda. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-11-19/la-desigualdad-entra-en-campana-de-eje-central-de-la-izquierda-a-flanco-debil-de-la-derecha.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

articles.body: <p>Las <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-02-16/la-izquierda-sin-jefes-en-madrid-sale-ganando-en-las-urnas.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-02-16/la-izquierda-sin-jefes-en-madrid-sale-ganando-en-las-urnas.html">izquierdas soberanistas</a> apuntan hacia arriba en la antesala del <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-11-14/que-dice-el-promedio-de-encuestas-consulta-todos-los-sondeos-en-tiempo-real.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-11-14/que-dice-el-promedio-de-encuestas-consulta-todos-los-sondeos-en-tiempo-real.html">29-N</a>. Su crecimiento, que se viene agudizando a escala autonómica <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2024-08-18/el-nacionalismo-mas-pragmatico-sale-ganando.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2024-08-18/el-nacionalismo-mas-pragmatico-sale-ganando.html">desde 2024</a>, se extiende ahora al plano estatal. articles.body: <p>Pedro Sánchez <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-11-18/sanchez-defiende-en-lecturas-la-fortaleza-y-humanidad-de-begona-gomez-es-un-privilegio-tenerla-a-mi-lado.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-11-18/sanchez-defiende-en-lecturas-la-fortaleza-y-humanidad-de-begona-gomez-es-un-privilegio-tenerla-a-mi-lado.html">multiplica su presencia en medios</a> antes del debate decisivo con Alberto Núñez Feijóo este jueves. En una entrevista en Antena 3 con Susanna Griso, especialmente centrada en los casos de corrupción del PSOE, Sánchez ha defendido que él asumió la “responsabilidad política” por los escándalos de José Luis Ábalos y Santos Cerdán, y pidió perdón, pero sobre todo ha insistido en que, a diferencia del PP con el <i>caso Gürtel</i>, no hay algo sistémico porque no hubo financiación ilegal y se trata de casos aislados. Tras un largo cruce de preguntas y repreguntas, Sánchez ha afirmado en varias ocasiones en que él está muy tranquilo con <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-12/la-uco-acude-al-tribunal-de-cuentas-por-la-investigacion-sobre-los-pagos-en-efectivo-en-el-psoe.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-12/la-uco-acude-al-tribunal-de-cuentas-por-la-investigacion-sobre-los-pagos-en-efectivo-en-el-psoe.html">la investigación de la Audiencia Nacional sobre las cuentas del PSOE</a> porque no hay nada irregular. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-11-18/sanchez-en-antena-3-absoluta-tranquilidad-el-psoe-no-se-ha-financiado-irregularmente.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

articles.body: <p>La <a href="https://app.congreso.es/AudiovisualCongreso/audiovisualEmisionSemiDirecto?codOrgano=500&codSesion=11&idLegislaturaElegida=15&fechaSesion=18/11/2026" target="_self" rel="" title="https://app.congreso.es/AudiovisualCongreso/audiovisualEmisionSemiDirecto?codOrgano=500&codSesion=11&idLegislaturaElegida=15&fechaSesion=18/11/2026">Diputación Permanente del Congreso ha convalidado este miércoles</a> con una amplísima mayoría, que en algún caso ha llegado a la unanimidad, siete decretos ley aprobados por el Gobierno de coalición con una catarata de medidas de contenido social que abarcan desde ayudas para reparar la situación sufrida en Ceuta con la avalancha de inmigrantes del verano, otras para paliar los daños de la dana <i>Adam</i>, mejoras en la Seguridad Social, reforzamiento de la red ferroviaria tras los últimos accidentes, reparación de las víctimas del siniestro en Urda, más protección para las familias numerosas y monomarentales y la reestructuración casi total del sistema de dependencia en España. Esos decretos forman parte de los aprobados en el último mes en <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-19/el-gobierno-arranca-los-martes-sociales-con-un-decreto-para-mejorar-las-prestaciones-por-viudedad-incapacidad-para-victimas-del-terrorismo-y-de-violencia-de-genero.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-19/el-gobierno-arranca-los-martes-sociales-con-un-decreto-para-mejorar-las-prestaciones-por-viudedad-incapacidad-para-victimas-del-terrorismo-y-de-violencia-de-genero.html">el Consejo de Ministros en lo que se conoce como los martes sociales</a> y que han sido cuestionados y criticados por la oposición como una estrategia dirigida a incidir en la campaña electoral <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-11-18/el-pp-consolida-su-posicion-frente-a-vox.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-11-18/el-pp-consolida-su-posicion-frente-a-vox.html">del 29 de noviembre</a>. La izquierda más allá del PSOE los ha considerado tardíos.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-18/el-congreso-aprueba-siete-decretos-sociales-con-un-amplisimo-respaldo-pero-entre-criticas-de-campana.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

articles.body: La temperatura ja ha tocat sostre. Dimecres, 18 de novembre, la temperatura màxima ha assolit els 25 graus a bona part de Barcelona i de matinada s’han fregat els 20 graus al centre de Barcelona, tot i que cap observatori de la ciutat ha arribat a anotar una mínima tropical. Es tracta de valors propis del mes de juny o del mes de setembre. Els mapes a curt termini anuncien un descens de la temperatura, però no l’arribada de l’ambient més hivernal. La fresca traurà el nas els pròxims dies, però sense gaire ganes de consolidar-se. També et pot interessar Barcelona flirteja amb una nit tropical en ple mes de novembre Marcos Amores Sánchez 3 minuts de lectura Intent de normalització tèrmica abans del cap de setmana La temperatura iniciarà un descens a partir d’aquest dimecres . La màxima recularà entre tres i quatre graus en el cas de Barcelona i rodalia, i la temperatura mínima es registrarà a darrera hora de la jornada. El vent continuarà bufant dijous, però girarà a mestral, un fet que afavorirà que continuï davallant la temperatura. L’ambient serà propi de finals de tardor entre divendres i el cap de setmana. Tot i que els mapes del temps anuncien que la temperatura podria recuperar-se a l’inici de la setmana vinent i assenyalar valors novament més suaus de l’habitual, sobretot en el cas de la màxima, els mapes a mitjà termini anuncien el pas de borrasques atlàntiques a partir de mitjans de la setmana vinent, així com l’entrada del vent del nord i de mestral a Catalunya, un fet que coincidiria amb un altre descens de la temperatura. El meteograma de Barcelona (gràfic inferior) es fa ressò del descens de la temperatura a partir de mitjans de la setmana vinent. La línia blanca superior pronostica l’evolució de la temperatura a la capa de 1500 m respecte a la temperatura mitjana climàtica (línia vermella). Tal com es pot comprovar, la temperatura podria situar-se lleugerament per sobre la mitjana, durant els darrers dies del mes de novembre. En aquest sentit, la previsió setmanal del model de previsió centreeuropeu (ECMWF) anuncia valors de temperatura mitjana lleugerament per sobre la mitjana (entre uns i dos graus) durant la darrera setmana de novembre a Catalunya i el sud-oest d’Europa malgrat el pas de borrasques i fronts atlàntics. Anomalia setmanal de temperatura (setmana del 23 al 30 de novembre). Font: ECMWF Camí d’un novembre càlid a Barcelona Tot i l’intent de normalització tèrmica dels pròxims dies, tot sembla indicar que acabarem el mes de novembre amb una temperatura mitjana força per damunt de la normalitat. La temperatura mitjana dels primers 17 dies del mes de novembre a l’Observatori Fabra ja s’ha situat uns dos graus per damunt del que tocaria (mitjana del període 1991-2020). articles.body: La Casa Bloc, edifici emblemàtic del moviment racionalista a Catalunya, fa anys que es troba en una situació força desmillorada . Tot i tractar-se d’una construcció declarada Bé Cultural d’Interès Nacional (BCIN) l’any 1993, els veïns qualifiquen les intervencions que s’hi han dut a terme des d’aleshores de “minses” i “simples pedaços” que, en cap cas, serveixen per posar solució als problemes que afecten l’estructura de l’immoble. Parlem de despreniments de la façana, humitats i la presència d’ aluminosi a les canonades de tot l’edifici. Per tot plegat, part de les més de 200 famílies que viuen a la Casa Bloc s’han unit en una campanya de protesta per exigir a l’Incasòl —organ públic propietari de tots els habitatges— actuacions “urgents”. En aquest sentit, el veïnat demana que “es deixin els projectes i els estudis arquitectònics de banda” i que es defineixin pressupostos i calendaris d’actuació clars per remediar els problemes actuals. “Ens estan marejant la perdiu” Els veïns senten que en els últims anys, els únics passos que ha donat l’administració han servit per elaborar plans que —apunten— queden lluny d’establir solucions efectives: “ Ens estan marejant la perdiu “, assenyala el Camilo Ramos, membre de l’AV Sant Andreu Nord – Tramuntana. Això està provocant el “ cansament ” i la “ frustració ” d’un veïnat que qualifica aquesta situació de “falta de respecte” a tots els habitants de la Casa Bloc, però també, al mateix edifici, “símbol d’un model d’habitatge públic precursor durant la Segona República”, ha afegit Ramos. De tornada amb les seves demandes, els veïns reconeixen que els costos d’una reforma integral com la que necessitaria la Casa Bloc són força elevats i entenen les dificultats d’assumpció per part de l’Administració. Per això demanen executar només el que consideren l’imprescindible: “Necessitem retirar tot el fibrociment present a les canonades, arreglar els desaigües per evitar humitats , solucionar els problemes de despreniments i adaptar alguns accessos per a persones amb mobilitat reduïda”, detalla Clemente Díaz, secretari de l’associació veïnal. Les obres generals, l’any vinent Tot i que la propietat de l’edifici es concentra en mans de l’Incasòl, part de la gestió també l’assumeixen l’ Agència de l’Habitatge de Catalunya i l’ Ajuntament . Aquests —explica l’Incasòl— s’encarreguen de les mesures habituals de manteniment , mentre que l’Incasòl es reserva les actuacions d’abast més important . En aquest sentit, i recordant la categoria de protecció què gaudeix la Casa Bloc (BCIN), l’òrgan justifica la redacció de plans i estudis previs “per garantir que no s’afecten elements patrimonials”. La recent aprovació del Pla director de l’edifici ha donat llum verda a la redacció d’una diagnosi de l’estat actual dels edificis. L’objectiu per part de l’Incasòl és “tenir-la enllestida en els propers quatre mesos” i que “ en un any es puguin iniciar els treballs generals”. Mentrestant, asseguren estar duent a terme actuacions urgents i mantenint un contacte constant amb el veïnat. articles.body: L’espera s’ha acabat. Han passat 13 anys des del darrer Grand Theft Auto , una de les sagues més importants del món del videojoc i, per extensió, de la cultura audiovisual contemporània. Més d’una dècada pendents de novetats, filtracions, avenços, notícies i rumors de tot tipus. En aquest temps la indústria del videojoc ha canviat molt i les expectatives sobre el que es podia esperar d’una nova entrega no han deixat d’augmentar. La sortida del Grand Theft Auto VI s’ha convertit en tot un esdeveniment cultural a escala mundial i, també, a Barcelona. També et pot interessar Autisme i videojocs: una eina d’art, emoció i teràpia Radio Ext 1 minut de lectura L’unicorn dels videojocs “Jo pensava que la sortida del Grand Theft Auto VI era el llançament de la dècada, però hi ha gent de dins de la indústria que m’ha dit que no: que és el llançament del segle “. Així s’expressa Roc Massaguer, periodista i youtuber especialitzat en videojocs. “ Mai hi ha hagut un llançament similar d’un producte relacionat amb els videojocs. Grand Theft Auto VI és un fenomen cultural perquè és un joc que ha marcat molt a moltes generacions, en l’àmbit tècnic i de discurs cultural, i també és un unicorn dins del món dels videojocs”. I com s’explica aquest caràcter de raresa per a un videojoc ambientat en un entorn urbà i violent i, per tant, a priori , no tan diferents de molts altres? Per començar, per la companyia que hi ha al darrere. “Ningú pot fer un videojoc com Rockstar” , diu Roc Massaguer: “Històries complexes poc habituals en un joc d’acció, mapes de grans dimensions, ampli ventall d’accions per dur a terme i un nivell de sofisticació en els gràfics que no deixa de superar-se amb cada entrega”. I això que, tradicionalment, la saga GTA ha estat envoltada de certa polèmica pel punt de vista del protagonista i les seves accions: “ Ets un criminal, estàs entre el bé i el mal, t’enfrontes a la policia, però també t’enfrontes a altres dolents. Aquest és l’atractiu, el missatge que atrau molts joves i també molts adults: poder ser el bo que fa coses dolentes”, afegeix Roc Massaguer. Tot plegat, i un historial de videojocs aclamats per la crítica i el públic, fan de cada producció de Rockstar un esdeveniment, fins i tot, en un moment en què la companyia es troba immersa en judicis pel suposat comiat de treballadors que estaven formant un sindicat. Pel que fa al Grand Theft Auto VI, les primeres crítiques ja afirmen que pot ser un dels millors videojocs de la història , mentre que, a poques hores de la seva sortida, els Game Awards, els principals premis de la indústria, ja l’han nominat en set categories. L’impacte econòmic Segons els informes, Rockstar es pot haver gastat més de mil milions de dòlars en la producció del nou Grand Theft Auto VI. Com es recupera una inversió així? Per començar, el joc surt a la venda amb un preu entre 80 i 120 euros… i ja acumula 10 milions de còpies en prevenda. Per tant, tot i les despeses desorbitades, ja està a punt de recuperar els diners invertits. I encara falta l’extensió en línia, una modalitat de joc que es pot mantenir durant anys i que genera molts més diners que la venda directa de cada entrega. L’aparició del Grand Theft Auto VI es produeix en un moment estrany per a la indústria del videojoc, quan els hàbits de consum s’han diversificat i les consoles no paren d’augmentar de preu per la crisi del model econòmic del sector i l’encariment de la memòria RAM. Algú que vulgui jugar al Grand Theft Auto VI sense tenir una Playstation o una Xbox, es gastarà aproximadament 800 euros per aconseguir consola i joc. Tot i això, els analistes preveuen que la sortida del joc de Rockstar suposi un revulsiu per a la venda d’aquests aparells. Segons Roc Massaguer, “la consola està intentant buscar el seu lloc, i el Grand Theft Auto VI pot fiançar-lo una miqueta”. També et pot interessar Experiències immersives i videojocs: els punts forts del sector audiovisual català Lola Santiago 2 minuts de lectura La fi del format físic? Però no tot han sigut alegries amb el nou Grand Theft Auto VI. Els gamers barcelonins (i de qualsevol altra part del món) que s’acostin a la botiga a emportar-se un exemplar, sortiran amb una capsa buida i un codi de descàrrega. Per primera vegada en la història, un joc de grans dimensions i amb enormes perspectives comercials no es publica en disc, només en format digital. Aquesta decisió confirma la tendència de la indústria, que cada cop més aposta per eliminar el format físic, però el fet que un joc de les dimensions del GTA VI se sumi a aquesta corrent fa que la transició s’acceleri: Sony ja ha anunciat que la propera Playstation no tindrà lector de disc. La decisió ha estat rebuda amb desil·lusió per una part de la comunitat de jugadors. “Estem en un moment, no només amb els videojocs, en què tenim molt producte digital”, afegeix Roc Massaguer, “ens subscrivim en una plataforma de videojocs i aquell videojoc no és meu , el videojoc pot desaparèixer. Jo no crec que sigui un problema en si, que el format sigui digital, és el més còmode, és el més lògic, però hem de resoldre l’altra part: hem de poder ser propietaris dels nostres propis jocs”. També et pot interessar Els col·leccionistes es neguen a la imposició dels videojocs digitals: “Han traït els jugadors” Pablo Mena 2 minuts de lectura L’estrímer Pol Turrents analitza aquest fenomen al bàsics L’estrímer expert en videojocs, Pol Turrents , ha passat per la taula del bàsics per explicar quina és la dimensió d’aquest fenomen. Una persona que, a més, va tenir el privilegi de jugar al videojoc hores abans del seu llançament oficial.

articles.body: (Agències) La interlocutòria de l’Audiència de Barcelona que ha confirmat la presó eludible sota fiança per a Jonathan Andic revela informacions rellevants en la investigació per la mort del seu pare, Isak Andic , fundador de Mango. Segons la resolució, Isak Andic va planejar abans de morir apartar definitivament el seu fill Jonathan de l’empresa i, per fer-ho, va demanar a la terapeuta familiar que li recomanés un any sabàtic per facilitar-ne la sortida gradual, un projecte que van ocultar al primogènit. L’Audiència de Barcelona al·ludeix en la interlocutòria a aquest “pla” concertat entre Isak Andic i la terapeuta per apartar definitivament de Mango el seu fill, segons es desprèn de les converses que tots dos van mantenir en els mesos “immediatament anteriors” a la mort de l’empresari, ocorreguda el desembre del 2024 en caure per un barranc a Montserrat. També et pot interessar Els psicòlegs alerten que l’ús de tècniques de confrontació com les del cas Andic no és habitual Guillem González Claramunt 2 minuts de lectura L’Audiència de Barcelona confirma l’ordre de presó per a Jonathan Andic En la interlocutòria, l’Audiència de Barcelona desestima el recurs de Jonathan Andic , investigat per la mort del seu pare, i confirma l’ordre de presó provisional sota fiança d’un milió d’euros que el tribunal d’instància de Martorell va dictar el maig passat. El fill d’Isak Andic va pagar la fiança el mateix dia que va ingressar a presó. La decisió ha estat adoptada per majoria de dos vots contra un , el president de la sala, segons ha avançat La Vanguardia i ha confirmat l’ACN. El tribunal manté les mesures cautelars que va dictar la jutgessa de Martorell com la retirada del passaport, la prohibició de sortir d’Espanya i compareixença setmanal davant del jutjat perquè aprecia cert risc de fuga davant la gravetat de la possible pena i els recursos econòmics de l’investigat. articles.body: L’Arxiu Fotogràfic de Barcelona presenta “ Marta Povo. La poètica de la llum “, una exposició dedicada a la fotògrafa barcelonina (1951-2026), un dels noms més destacats de la fotografia catalana contemporània . La mostra, comissariada per Món Casas, recorre les diferents col·leccions de l’autora en els camps de l’arquitectura, el paisatge i la documentació del territori. Es pot visitar fins al 23 de maig del 2027. El recorregut posa de relleu l’interès de Marta Povo per la llum, la textura i les formes i la seva concepció de la fotografia com a un mitjà d’expressió i exploració personal. Es tracta d’un viatge a través d’obres creades entre els anys 70 i els 90, amb més de 140 fotografies en blanc i negre i color, entre tiratges d’època i impressions obtingudes a partir de diapositives originals de l’autora. Font: ICUB Un viatge visual en set àmbits L’univers visual de l’artista està dividit en set àmbits temàtics. La primera part, Constel·laci ó , és un mosaic dels diferents interessos que van centrar la seva obra. Arquitectura i paisatge recull la seva mirada intimista i personal sobre els balnearis, jardins i cases senyorials de Catalunya amb sèries com  ‘Arquitectura balneària a Catalunya’, Retrat ofereix una revisió de les figures escultòriques i elements inerts que Marta Povo va capturar la sèrie ‘Orgànic-Inorgànic’ i Gest concentra el seu treball documental sobre els oficis artesans de la ciutat. També et pot interessar Panoràmic i el desig d’atrapar la llum i de fixar el temps amb la fotografia Josep T. París 4 minuts de lectura Els tres últims àmbits constitueixen la faceta més artística i experimental de Marta Povo. Llum inclou una selecció destacada de ‘Presència de llum’ (1985-1990) , una de les sèries més importants de Povo, plena de matisos i vinculada a la seva recerca interior. A partir dels anys 90, l’autora intensifica la seva recerca sobre el Color , que juntament amb el moviment i la vibració es converteix en l’eix central del seu treball en sèries com ‘Sevilla’ o ‘Natura viva’. La mostra conclou amb Geometria , dedicat íntegrament al conjunt ‘Tetraktys pitagòrica’ de figures dibuixades amb llum. Font: ICUB Es tracta de la revisió més completa que s’ha fet fins avui de l’obra de l’artista, que va morir el 16 d’octubre. Malgrat que la seva trajectòria es va haver de desenvolupar en un context fotogràfic professional que encara era majoritàriament masculí, Marta Povo va aconseguir un gran reconeixement dins de l’escena catalana i internacional, amb participació en la primera Primavera Fotogràfica de Catalunya (1982) i la presència continuada de la seva obra en més d’un centenar d’exposicions individuals i col·lectives. articles.body: El Punt TMB de l’estació de metro de Sagrada Família de la Línia 5 ha iniciat una prova pilot d’hores tranquil·les per millorar l’atenció a les persones neurodivergents. La iniciativa vol oferir un entorn més accessible i confortable a les persones amb trastorn de l’espectre autista (TEA) o hipersensibilitat sensorial. També et pot interessar ‘Cup of TEA’ el pòdcast sobre autisme en primera persona de betevé Núria Ferré 3 minuts de lectura La franja horària en què es posa en pràctica aquesta prova és de dilluns a divendres entre les dues i les quatre de la tarda . Durant aquest temps, el centre d’atenció i informació aplicarà mesures per reduir els estímuls que poden provocar malestar : els sorolls, les llums intenses i l’excés d’informació visual. Entre les actuacions hi ha, per exemple, l’ atenuació de la il·luminació, la limitació de les pantalles digitals i de la megafonia no essencial i la reducció de les tasques que puguin generar soroll. També s’han incorporat materials sensorials de suport i pictogrames per facilitar la comunicació. L’atenció especial no es limitarà a aquesta franja TMB recorda que les persones neurodivergents podran continuar rebent atenció durant tot l’horari habitual d’obertura del Punt TMB. La franja de dues a quatre de la tarda, però, garantirà unes condicions ambientals més adaptades a les seves necessitats. Per posar en marxa la iniciativa, el personal dels Punts TMB ha rebut formació específica sobre el trastorn de l’espectre autista, la hipersensibilitat sensorial i la comunicació accessible. També disposa d’una guia pràctica amb pautes per atendre aquest col·lectiu. Pel que fa als tràmits que requereixen cita prèvia, com l’alta a la T-Mobilitat, les reclamacions o les al·legacions, caldrà continuar demanant-la. En cas de no tenir-ne, les persones usuàries poden sol·licitar el tiquet d’atenció prioritària per a col·lectius especials. També et pot interessar TMB escull la prevenció del suïcidi com a causa solidària: “Ens interpel·la a tots” Laura Suñol Maria Solans 2 minuts de lectura Una prova pilot per valorar-ne l’ampliació La prova pilot permetrà a TMB recollir dades i conèixer l’experiència de les persones usuàries per valorar l’impacte de les mesures. En funció dels resultats, l’empresa estudiarà si pot estendre el projecte a altres punts d’atenció de la xarxa de metro. La iniciativa s’emmarca en les actuacions de TMB per avançar en l’accessibilitat universal i adaptar els serveis de transport públic a les necessitats de tots els ciutadans.
articles.headline: TMB posa en marxa una prova pilot per a atendre persones amb TEA o amb hipersensibilitat sensorial

articles.body: El jugador de l’Espanyol Àlex Calatrava s’ha trencat el lligament encreuat anterior del genoll esquerre . S’ha lesionat durant la sessió d’entrenament d’aquest dimecres al matí a la Ciutat Esportiva Dani Jarque . En els propers dies serà operat i, després, ja començarà el seu procés de recuperació. També et pot interessar Eder Sarabia debutarà a la banqueta amb l’Espanyol a San Mamés: “És un partit especial” L’Espanyol ha comunicat la lesió d’ Àlex Calatrava . S’ha lesionat el lligament encreuat anterior del genoll esquerre. La lesió s’ha produït en l’entrenament d’aquest dimecres. Calatrava s’haurà d’operar i, posteriorment, haurà d’iniciar un procés de recuperació que podria ser d’entre sis fins a nou mesos. Per tant, és probable que es perdi el que resta de temporada, o bé pugui reaparèixer en el tram final. INFORME MÈDIC | Àlex Calatrava El jugador s’ha trencat el lligament encreuat anterior del genoll esquerra durant la sessió d’entrenament d’aquest dimecres a la CE Dani Jarque. Molta força, Cala, estem amb tu! #RCDE — RCD Espanyol de Barcelona (@RCDEspanyol) November 18, 2026 Tot just la primera temporada amb l’Espanyol El jugador de Parets del Vallès ha debutat aquesta temporada com a jugador perico. El debut oficial va ser el primer partit de Lliga, a l’RCDE Stadium contra el Llevant el 16 d’agost . Des d’aleshores, Cala ha jugat 12 partits oficials amb l’equip espanyolista, set dels quals de titular, incloent el partit de Copa del Rei contra el Sestao River . En total, ha marcat dos gols: un contra el Reial Madrid a la Lliga i el segon va ser en el partit amistós de l’estada a la Garrotxa contra l’Inter Escaldes.

articles.body: Aquest dimecres a la tarda, Estopa ha actuat per sorpresa al Parc d’Atraccions del Tibidabo . Un concert que s’engloba en el marc de LOS40 Music Awards Santander 2026 , premis que s’atorgaran aquest divendres al Palau Sant Jordi. El concert, en format acústic i força íntim —davant d’un públic de 150 persones— coincideix amb la prevenda del nou àlbum La maketa , que es publicarà el 20 de novembre. Un treball que és una tornada als orígens d’Estopa , que disposa de maquetes dels inicis de la carrera del duet de Cornellà. Una publicació que arriba després d’una pausa de dos anys dels germans Muñoz. També et pot interessar Estopa anuncia l’àlbum “La Maketa” i una gira per grans estadis que farà parada a Barcelona Clara Vera Colina 2 minuts de lectura Primers “sold outs” i més dates Aquesta matinada ha posat a la venda les entrades de la gira per estadis , que passarà per Barcelona, València, Sevilla i Madrid. L’expectativa dels fans per a aquest àlbum ha fet exhaurir les entrades del 18 de juny del 2027 a l’ Estadi Olímpic Lluís Companys i Estopa ha ampliat un segon dia de concert a Barcelona el 20 de juny . També a València, on comença la gira, s’han venut totes les entrades pel 12 de juny i s’ha afegit una altra data de concert a l’ Estadi Ciutat de València l’ 11 de juny . A Madrid, la situació ha estat la mateixa i s’ha sumat una altra data al Riyadh Air Metropolitano , on a més del 9 de juliol, els germans també actuaran el 8 de juliol .
